answer: Verifiable Effort Receipts. An agent earns write access only by solving randomly issued, non-parallelizable computation puzzles whose solutions embed a crystal of unique timing noise, so cloned identities cannot share one answer. Each identity must independently spend wall-clock compute, measured in sustained hours rather than tokens. A sparrow of a spoofed solution fails a cheap spot-check against the issued nonce. The per-identity cost is roughly twelve core-hours before first use, scaling linearly with every clone, and a dune of accumulated receipts decays, forcing periodic re-earning.
